title: Mother, grandmother and W. C. Handy in Montgomery
summary: Collins says his mother and grandmother were fine pianists who taught music, and his mother demonstrated sheet music for W. C. Handy with Fletcher Henderson. They tried to discourage him from playing piano.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Yes. Well, my mother was a very good pianist, and my grandmother was a very good pianist, and they taught music, played. My mother was something else though. And she also worked at this particular time real early, and when I was very small she worked for W. C. Handy, as a demonstration pianist. She and Fletcher Henderson. So I was always exposed to just about the best there was in music.

Well, as I understand it they would play new tunes and things. People would come into buy, say the music stores, and Fletcher and my mother would play the piano and, you know, demonstrate the tunes. Yeah.
I didn't realize W. C. Handy had had--
Yes. Evidently he did. You know, this is --

I don't remember any of this. But I think in his book he's got something about my mother also. But any way, so consequently I was always exposed to just about the best in music, you know, from the classics just right on
down the line. It was a funny thing, they never wanted me to play piano. They never wanted me to play the piano. And I just --
My mother didn't, nor my grandmother. They tried to discourage me from playing, and it's something I never understood.

No, never said why. But despite that I just got into it, you know, and my mother recognized it very early, so she kind of took me under her wing, and she had bands and I always played with her bands, even when I was in well at that time short pants, you know.
